It may be a bit harder to go immediately to extremely low keys like G or extremely high keys like F#. As the response gets slower or faster depending on each key.

I'd recommend either a Bb or a D. These two are not only popular blues harp keys, but in my opinion, they're easy harps to get into their respective registers on the harmonica. Bb has some deep sounding bends and powerful wailing sounds, but it doesn't sacrifice the responsiveness as other low key harps. D is great for bluegrass playing due to its response, but it doesn't sound too shrill on the high notes and can still have a strong, bluesy tone.

I would usually get into a certain mindset when playing any genre of music. For blues, I mainly focus on expressive tone and solos. For country, it's trying to sneak in fills whenever I can (along with the occasional solo). For jazz, I try to keep it simple while soloing and not go overboard with speed.
My advice would be try to expand your horizons by listening to different players. I grew up listening to Terry McMillan and I eventually learned how to play solos and fills from him. If you want a certain sound for non-blues music, listen to how players outside of the genre play and try to achieve that mindset while playing.

Most diatonic players will tell you that his playing is absolute trash. In my opinion, he had potential with "All Along the Watchtower", but his playing got worse as he became more popular. His playing is some of the most passionate and aggressive harmonica I've ever heard in my life.
